clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year post-kidney transplant patient on chronic immunosuppression (prednisone 20 mg/day and sodium mycophenolate 5.760 mg/day) presented with a one-year history of two subcutaneous nodules (approximately 2 cm each, firm, painful, barely delimited, adherent, with erythematous and cyanotic overlying skin) on the right arm and left forearm, accompanied by systemic symptoms of fever, cough, and weight loss that began simultaneously with nodule onset. Biopsy of the right arm nodule revealed cellular tissue with macrophage proliferation, multinucleated giant cells, and lymphoplasma neutrophilic infiltrate. Methenamine silver staining demonstrated abundant intracytoplasmic microorganisms characteristic of Histoplasma capsulatum, sometimes forming hyphae and spores. One year after symptom onset, the patient received the diagnosis and treatment for disseminated histoplasmosis.
